name: Social Determinants of Health
title: Social Determinants of Health
answer: Social determinants of health are the conditions in which people are born, grow, live, work and age, including income, housing, education, employment, food access, transportation and neighborhood safety. In epidemiology and population health they are treated as upstream drivers of disease risk and health inequity, distinct from clinical care and from genetics. Work in this area asks how these conditions distribute across populations and how they shape outcomes such as life expectancy, chronic disease and maternal health. It sits alongside clinical medicine as the part of health that happens outside the clinic.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Social determinants of health are the conditions in which people are born, grow, live, work and age, including income, housing, education, employment, food access, transportation and neighborhood safety. In epidemiology and population health they are treated as upstream drivers of disease risk and health inequity, distinct from clinical care and from genetics. Work in this area asks how these conditions distribute across populations and how they shape outcomes such as life expectancy, chronic disease and maternal health. It sits alongside clinical medicine as the part of health that happens outside the clinic.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The data foundation is administrative and survey records: census and American Community Survey tables, vital statistics, disease registries, electronic health records, insurance claims, and municipal datasets on housing, transit and environmental quality. These sources are joined at the geographic level, often by census tract or ZIP code, using geographic information systems and geocoding. Because the data are heterogeneous and inconsistently coded, much of the infrastructure work is harmonization, linkage and missing data handling. Privacy rules such as HIPAA and small-cell suppression constrain what can be released or shared.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Analysts use regression and multilevel models to separate area-level effects from individual-level ones, and causal methods such as difference in differences, instrumental variables and propensity score matching where policy changes or natural experiments allow. Machine learning is used for prediction and for clustering neighborhoods by risk profile, and increasingly for extracting social risk signals from clinical notes. Indexes such as the Area Deprivation Index and the Social Vulnerability Index aggregate many indicators into a single score. Validation matters, since a model trained in one city or health system may not transfer to another.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The main risks are re-identification of individuals in small areas, stigmatizing or redlining communities through predictive scores, and encoding historical bias when past inequities are used as training labels. Provenance requires documenting data sources, geographic resolution, collection dates and known gaps, since a tract-level measure can hide wide variation within it. Consent and community engagement are expected when data describe identifiable groups, and some datasets carry use agreements that limit redistribution.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward integrating social risk data into clinical workflows and population health dashboards, so that screening for food insecurity or housing instability becomes routine and actionable. Better linkage across health, housing and social service systems is the central technical ambition, alongside methods that move from correlation to credible causal claims. Community-based participatory approaches and equity audits of models are gaining ground as a counterweight to purely predictive uses. The unresolved questions are how to act on a social risk once it is measured, and who is accountable when the underlying condition is not something a health system controls.
